item.title: A Counterexample to Three Conjectures of Luo
item.description: arXiv:2610.13979v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a single counterexample to Conjectures 1--3 as stated in Luo's paper: a minimal two-tetrahedron triangulation of the lens space L(3,1) with a null-homotopic loop edge. The proof uses quadrilateral matching equations, an explicit calculation of shape parameters, and known results on volume maximization.
item.dc:creator: Qilong Guo

item.title: Tight surgeries on torus knots
item.description: arXiv:2610.14218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a complete classification of tight contact structures on manifolds obtained from any surgery along any torus knot, which provides the first such classification on an infinite family of knots. The main tools are the classification of non-loose torus knots, bordered contact invariants via their immersed curve interpretations, and non-thickenable tori in knot complements. As a byproduct of this classification, we also give the first classification of contact structures on some surface bundles over the circle with fibers of genus larger than $1$. The symplectic fillability of these contact structures is also studied and leads to, among other things, the disproof of a conjecture of Ghiggini and Van Horn-Morris on Stein fillability of some contact structures on a Brieskorn sphere.
item.dc:creator: John B. Etnyre, Hyunki Min, B\"ulent Tosun, Konstantinos Varvarezos

item.title: Shake concordance in the topological concordance class of the Hopf link
item.description: arXiv:2610.14575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Within the topological concordance class of the Hopf link, we construct infinitely many classes under the equivalence relation generated by smooth $0$-shake concordance. Each contains infinitely many smooth concordance classes represented by links that are pairwise strongly $0$-shake concordant and whose second components have unbounded smooth slice genus.
item.dc:creator: Weizhe Shen

item.title: Boundary of Anosov coaffine representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.14897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Gamma \le \mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb R)$ be a torsion-free hyperbolic group dividing a properly and strictly convex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb R\mathrm P^d$, and let $\rho: \Gamma \to \mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb R)$ be the inclusion. We study representations of $\Gamma$ into the coaffine group that are deformations of $\rho\oplus 1 \in \mathrm{Hom}(\Gamma, \mathrm{GL}(d+2,\mathbb R))$ and that lie on the boundary of the locus of projective Anosov representations. In this setting, we identify a canonical limit set $\Lambda$ for the action and study its fine geometric features which are, in a suitable sense, stable. We prove the existence of an ending lamination that encodes the failure of the Anosov condition and the non-existence of a Cannon--Thurston map. Under certain conditions, we compute the Hausdorff dimension and show that the corresponding measure is positive.
item.dc:creator: Marit Bobb, James Farre

item.title: One boundary, infinitely geometries
item.dc:creator: Jiming Ma

item.title: Symplectic four-manifolds and hyperbolic $\pi$-orbifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.15698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct closed symplectic 4-manifolds admitting the structure of hyperbolic $\pi$-orbifold, addressing LeBrun's conjecture. Our simplest example has Euler characteristic $304$, is tessellated by $64$ copies of the right-angled hyperbolic $120$-cell and admits a four-fold branched covering over a product of two surfaces of genus $4$.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Lin, Bruno Martelli

item.title: The inf spectrum of moduli space
item.description: arXiv:2610.15926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a surface of genus $g \geq 2$, its inf spectrum is the ordered multiset of inf lengths of curves on the surface, the infimum being over all hyperbolic metrics. We show that the inf spectrum has exponential growth with coefficients that only depend on g, improving the earlier double exponential upper bound. The proof involves developing a number of tools including the process of "thickening" a surface and the notion of model surfaces. These tools may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Ara Basmajian, Sayantika Mondal, Hugo Parlier

item.title: On infinite knot families with the same HOMFLYPT polynomial
item.description: arXiv:2610.16017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we focus on the examples constructed by Kanenobu and provide new family knots with the same HOMFLYPT polynomial invariants, which are distinguished by the Kauffman polynomial.
item.dc:creator: Yuki Matsushima

item.title: Loop Fundamental Quandles: A Geometric Generalization of the Knot Quandle
item.description: arXiv:2610.16056v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The knot quandle, introduced independently by Joyce and Matveev, admits a geometric description in terms of nooses. Motivated by this description, we introduce the \textit{loop fundamental quandle} $LQ(X,A,\ast)$ of a pair $(X,A)$ with a fixed base point $\ast\in X$. Its elements are represented by pairs consisting of a loop in $A$ and a path joining the base point of the loop to the fixed base point $\ast$. More generally, for a loop condition $P$ on $A$, invariant under free homotopy, we define the loop fundamental quandle $LQ(X,A,\ast;P)$. We establish functoriality and homotopy invariance of the loop fundamental quandle and show that it admits a natural augmented quandle structure over $\pi_1(X,\ast)$. For a knot $K$ in $S^3$, applying the construction to its exterior gives the \textit{knot loop quandle} $LQ(K,\ast;P)$. Appropriate choices of the loop condition recover the knot quandle, its $n$-th power quandles, and the full knot quandle. The construction is inspired by Joyce's noose-theoretic approach, but allows loop data that need not arise as the boundary of a disk satisfying the noose condition.
item.dc:creator: Seiichi Kamada

item.title: Lens spaces that cannot be obtained by two integral surgeries
item.description: arXiv:2610.16431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we demonstrate that there exists an infinite family of lens spaces L(p,q) that cannot be obtained from the 3-sphere by two integral surgeries. The first such lens space in our family is L(177,29).
item.dc:creator: Marco Golla, Marc Kegel

item.title: An Algebraic Matching Algorithm for the Genus of Grid Diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2610.16514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Grid diagrams encode knots and links combinatorially through an (n,n) winding matrix W(G). A fundamental invariant of the grid diagram is its genus g(G), which records essential topological information about the underlying knot. We give an algebraic algorithm that computes g(G) directly from W(G). The method repurposes the Hungarian algorithm ,after a column normalization that makes the matrix non-negative, it applies row-column reductions and minimum-vertex-cover corrections until the zero entries admit a perfect matching, equivalently until the minimum marking number equals n. By Konig's theorem the resulting permutation defines a distinguished grid state, and g(G) is then read from this matrix via the classical grid homology formula (Ozsvath-Stipsicz-Szabo). The novelty of this paper is the algorithm and its strongly polynomial analysis; the underlying invariant is known grid-homology theory. We illustrate the method on the trefoil and additional examples, and discuss extensions to (m,n) matrices and grid-move navigation toward the knot genus g(K).
item.dc:creator: Jun Wang, Shasha Yang

item.title: Knot Floer homology of fibered positive links
item.description: arXiv:2610.16539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the Maslov-graded next-to-top term of knot Floer homology for fibered positive links. Its rank in Maslov grading (-1) is the number of nontrivial prime connected-sum factors plus the number of components minus one, and the remaining summand is supported in Maslov grading zero. For a knot, the dimension of this remaining summand is determined by its Alexander polynomial. The proof combines a preferred-crossing construction with reductions of generalized Seifert surfaces to planar pretzel surfaces and a graded skein induction. We also obtain bounds on the fixed points of monodromies for fibered positive knots.
item.dc:creator: Zhechi Cheng

item.title: The symmetry group of Turk's head knots
item.description: arXiv:2610.16600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For p, q >= 3 with gcd(p,q) = 1 we show that the symmetry group of the Turk's head knot Th(p,q), the closure of the braid (sigma_1 sigma_2^{-1} sigma_3 sigma_4^{-1} ... sigma_{p-1}^{+-1})^q, is the dihedral group of order 4q. This proves Conjecture R of Di Prisa and \c{S}avk for q >= 3; the case p = 3 is due to Sakuma and Weeks. The argument is diagrammatic: by the flyping theorem of Menasco and Thistlethwaite, the symmetries of a knot with a prime, reduced alternating diagram without non-trivial flypes are the symmetries of the diagram (we write out a proof for the diagrams at hand), and we show that the standard diagram of Th(p,q) has no non-trivial flypes and exactly 4q symmetries. The chirality of Th(p,q) for even p, which also follows from a theorem of Murasugi, is visible in the group. We compare the argument with the geometric one of Sakuma and Weeks for p = 3.
item.dc:creator: Werner Stanggassinger

item.title: Homotopy Self-Equivalences of $\mathbb{R}P^2\times S^2$ and a Braid for non-orientable $4$-Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.16606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the group of based homotopy classes of self-homotopy equivalences of the non-orientable $4$-manifold $\RP^2\times S^2$. It is an elementary abelian $2$-group of rank $5$. The subgroup of classes whose based lift to the universal cover $S^2\times S^2$ has degree $+1$ has rank $4$ and is isomorphic to the group of free homotopy classes. The group maps onto the group of self-equivalences of the algebraic $2$-type, which has order $8$, with kernel $\pi_4(\RP^2\times S^2)\cong(\Z/2)^2$ generated by pinch-fold maps; that these maps are independent is shown by an adjunction argument. We then construct a non-orientable analogue of the Hambleton--Kreck braid of exact sequences in dimension $4$, for non-orientable manifolds with spin universal cover, stated for finite fundamental group. We apply the braid to $\RP^2\times S^2$ and to $\RP^4$, and for the Hambleton--Hillman manifold with fundamental group $(\Z/2)^2$ we determine the normal $1$-type and show that self-equivalences act on $\pi_2$ through diagonal sign matrices. For $\RP^2\times S^2$ the pinch-fold maps are detected by twisted spin bordism, and, assuming facts from surgery theory stated as hypotheses, exactly one of the three non-trivial pinch-fold maps is homotopic to a homeomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Mehmetcik Pamuk

item.title: On Intersection of Character Varieties Associated to Dehn Fillings of the Whitehead Link and Its Generalization
item.description: arXiv:2610.16731v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The canonical component of the character variety of a hyperbolic 2-bridge link complement M is an algebraic surface, from the work of Thurston. If we fix a boundary component T of M and perform a Dehn-filling on T, we get a 1-cusped manifold whose character variety is commonly a generalized curve that is naturally embedded in the character variety of M. If we perform distinct Dehn-fillings on M, we get various generalized curves on the canonical surface. In this paper, we analyze how these curves intersect with each other in the surface and study the topological implications for these intersection points. We also classify the intersection points that correspond to reducible characters, using the twisted Alexander polynomials associated to the Dehn-fillings. Throughout the paper, we use the Whitehead link as a motivating example to illustrate our core methodology, while some generalizations to other 2-bridge links will also be discussed.
item.dc:creator: Jiayu Wan, Charles Katerba

item.title: Morita Invariance of Saturated and Split Subgroupoids for Orbifold Embeddings
item.description: arXiv:2610.16885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Borzellino and Brunsden introduced a general notion of suborbifold and proved that a suborbifold is the image of a complete orbifold embedding if and only if it is both saturated and split. Their definitions and proofs are formulated in the classical language of orbifold charts. In this paper we translate these notions into the language of proper \'etale Lie groupoids.We introduce the groupoid analogues of saturation and splitting, which we call \emph{orbit saturation} and \emph{stabilizer splitting}, and prove that they coincide with the chart-based conditions. Our main theorem states that a subgroupoid is the image of a complete orbifold embedding if and only if it is both orbit saturated and stabilizer split. We then prove that these notions are Morita invariant: if two orbifold groupoids are Morita equivalent, then their orbit saturated and stabilizer split subgroupoids correspond naturally to each other. This solves an open problem raised by Mestre and Weilandt and explains why the embedding definition of Cho--Hong--Shin fails to be Morita invariant. Along the way we provide detailed examples, including the diagonal embedding, the non-split example of Borzellino and Brunsden, and explicit Morita equivalences.
item.dc:creator: Zhenxi Huang, Keyin Chen

item.title: Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations for Finsler metrics on symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations are random tessellations that arise as limits of Voronoi diagrams for Poisson point processes as their intensity tends to zero. For the Riemannian metric on a symmetric space of higher rank, Fr\k{a}czyk, Mellick, and Wilkens (arXiv:2307.01194) proved that the corresponding ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellation is almost surely completely connected, with an unbounded side between any two cells. This contrasts sharply with the geometry of ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces studied by D'Achille, Curien, Enriquez, Lyons, and \"Unel (arXiv:2303.16831). In this paper we introduce and study ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations for Finsler metrics on higher rank symmetric spaces. We show that ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations with respect to polyhedral Finsler metrics can exhibit either behavior seen in these previous works: generically they resemble the hyperbolic case, where almost surely all cells have bounded sides. We further introduce the ideal Selberg--Poisson--Voronoi tessellation of the space of positive definite symmetric matrices, which has particularly nice properties.
item.dc:creator: Colin Davalo, J. Maxwell Riestenberg, Anna Wienhard

item.title: Turaev cobracket, synthetic geometry and applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.17235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A teardrop geodesic on a hyperbolic surface is a closed curve that is geodesic except at exactly one point, called its vertex. One imagines a closed curve with one point held down as it deforms to a geodesic. For each teardrop geodesic, we give an explicit geometric construction of the closed geodesic in its free homotopy class. This construction also yields a relation between the length of the teardrop geodesic, the angle at its vertex, and the length of its geodesic representative. We then apply the construction to a self-intersecting closed geodesic at a chosen self-intersection point. Since, at that point, the geodesic splits into two directed teardrop geodesics, our construction gives a geometric description of Turaev's cobracket in terms of geodesic representatives. Using this description we prove that if two self-intersection points yield a pair of canceling terms in the cobracket, then the angle at these points and the lengths of the small loops determined are the same.
item.dc:creator: Moira Chas, Arpan Kabiraj

item.title: Point Processes and Gap Statistics for Translation Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the behavior of saddle connection directions on translation surfaces from the point process viewpoint. We define a direction point process for saddle connections of length at most $R>0$ on every translation surface. Given a general ergodic $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)$-invariant measure $\mu$ on a stratum of translation surfaces, we also define a slope point process associated with $\mu$. By utilizing the dynamics and geometry of strata, we show that for almost every translation surface, the direction point processes, rescaled by $R^2$, converge in distribution to the slope point process as $R\to\infty$. Using Palm distribution theory, we prove the existence of limiting joint gap distributions and obtain new regularity results for gap distributions associated with the general $\mu$. Finally, we study how these point processes and joint gap distributions behave as the genus $g$ tends to infinity. In the principal stratum, we show that the slope point processes, rescaled by $g^2$, converge in distribution to a Poisson point process. By passing to the corresponding Palm distributions, we show that the rescaled slope gaps converge jointly to independent exponential random variables, which is in stark contrast to the known non-exponential gap distributions in a fixed genus.
item.dc:creator: Kai Fu, Anthony Sanchez

item.title: Purely non-free actions on Riemann surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A group of conformal automorphisms of a Riemann surface is said to act purely non-free, or to produce a gpnf-action, if each of its finite-order elements has fixed points. It is known that every finite group admits a gpnf-action on a suitable closed Riemann surface of genus at least two. If $G$ is an infinite countable group, and $X$ is an infinite-type orientable surface, without planar ends and whose space of ends is self-similar, then we observe that there is a Riemann surface structure on $X$ admitting a gpnf-action by $G$. We obtain upper bounds for those finite groups producing a gpnf-action on a closed Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$. If $G$ is a finite group, then its purely non-free genus $\sigma^{pnf}_{hyp}(G)$ is the minimum genus of at least two of a closed Riemann surface admitting a gpnf-action by $G$. This parameter is already known for cyclic, abelian non-cyclic groups, ${\mathcal A}_{4}$, ${\mathcal A}_{5}$ and ${\mathfrak S}_{4}$. For general $G$, we provide the value of $\sigma^{pnf}_{hyp}(G)$, correcting a previous statement on this value. In particular, we observe that every genus is the purely non-free genus of some group. As an application, we describe the minimal purely non-free actions for the family of metacyclic groups $G^{0}_{s}(n)=\langle x,y: x^{n}=y^{2}=1, yxy=x^{s}\rangle,$ where $n \geq 3$ and $2 \leq s \leq n-1$ is such that $s^{2} \equiv 1 \mod(n)$.
item.dc:creator: Rub\'en A. Hidalgo, Jhony S. Leyca

item.title: $3$-manifold groups are linear
item.description: arXiv:2610.17608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the fundamental group of every compact graph $3$-manifold is linear over the complex numbers. As a corollary, all fundamental groups of compact $3$-manifolds are linear over the complex numbers.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolei Wu, Shengkui Ye

item.title: A parity constraint on the topological numbers of self-complementary triply-periodic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.18416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The stability zone of Novikov's problem of planar sections of triply periodic surfaces are labeled by indivisible triples of integers, which we call the soul of the zone. Which triples may occur is not known. We show that, if a Morse function $f$ on $\mathbb T^3$ admits a translation $\tau(x)=x+v$ with $f\circ\tau=-f$, so that the sets $\{f<0\}$ and $\{f>0\}$ are congruent, then in the generic genus-$3$ situation every topological number $L$ satisfies $\langle L,2v\rangle\equiv1\pmod2$. The mechanism is that the electron/hole type of a null-homologous closed trajectory is invariant under the period lattice and is reversed by $\tau$. For $f=\cos2\pi x+\cos2\pi y+\cos2\pi z$ and the $\mu$-cube, this means that the sum of the components of each soul is odd.
item.dc:creator: Roberto De Leo

item.title: A proof of the framed LMOV conjecture for links
item.description: arXiv:2610.18618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Labastida--Mari\~no--Ooguri--Vafa conjecture for oriented links with arbitrary integer framings. Consequently, the framed reformulated invariants have finite integral LMOV expansions for every integer framing vector.
item.dc:creator: Kefeng Liu, Pan Peng, Shengmao Zhu

item.title: Stably exotic knotted surfaces up to equivalence
item.description: arXiv:2610.18783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this short note we show the existence of stably exotic knotted surfaces in 4-manifolds in the sense that the embedded surfaces are topologically equivalent but are not smoothly equivalent even after any number of internal and external stabilisations.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Galvin, Daniel Kasprowski

item.title: The Links--Gould polynomial of an alternating link is alternating
item.description: arXiv:2610.18803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building on work of Kauffman--Saleur and earlier work of the second author, we derive a determinant formula for the Links--Gould polynomial of links. As an application, we prove a 20-year-old conjecture of Ishii: for any alternating link, the Links--Gould invariant is an alternating polynomial.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Harper, Ben-Michael Kohli

item.title: Arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds with bounded rank
item.description: arXiv:2610.18841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that closed arithmetic hyperbolic $n$-manifolds of bounded rank have bounded adjoint trace field degree, and consequently have lower bounded injectivity radius. From this, we obtain a number of corollaries. In particular, we obtain that closed arithmetic hyperbolic $3$-manifolds of bounded rank are contained in finitely many commensurability classes, and describe these commensurability classes. Additionally, it follows that for closed arithmetic hyperbolic $3$-manifolds, Heegaard genus is equal to rank for all but finitely many manifolds of each rank.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Zevenbergen

item.title: Localization of Floer homology for $\mathbb{Z}_p$-actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.14468v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For an odd prime $p$, we prove a Smith inequality over $\mathbb{F}_p$ for exact Lagrangian Floer homology under a symplectic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-action, assuming an equivariant stable normal trivialization compatible with the Lagrangians and the required relative Pin data. As an application, we obtain a rank inequality between the symplectic Khovanov homology of a $p$-periodic link and that of its quotient. These results extend the involutive localization of Seidel and Smith. The main construction is a stabilized chain complex. At every invariant intersection point we adjoin the Morse complex of a finite-dimensional normal spectral sphere, whose generators lie in free $\mathbb{Z}_p$-orbits. The differential counts holomorphic strips coupled to sphere half-trajectories by a one-sided weighted asymptotic evaluation. We prove transversality, a uniform spectral cutoff, and the compactification and gluing statements needed for the chain identity. The stabilized complex is quasi-isomorphic to the ordinary Floer complex and contains the complex of the fixed data as a subcomplex with free quotient, so the algebraic Smith inequality applies.
item.dc:creator: Erkao Bao, Tyler Lawson, Cheuk Yu Mak

item.title: Continuum-many discontinuous actions of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.15653v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For any $n\geq 1$, we construct a continuum of non-conjugate actions by homeomorphisms of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on the $n$-sphere $S^{n}$ that do not extend to a continuous action of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{R})$. We do this by adapting a blow-up construction of Bowden and Mann. We motivate studying these actions and note down some related observations.
item.dc:creator: Segev Gonen Cohen

item.title: A Sharp Lower Bound for Integral Menger Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.15981v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that round circles $C_L$ are the unique minimisers of integral Menger curvature among embedded closed $C^1$ curves $\gamma$ of prescribed length $L$ for every $p\geq 2$, i.e. $M_p(C_L) \leq M_p(\gamma)$, with equality if and only if $\gamma$ parametrises a round circle. The proof combines a three-point symmetrisation, an analysis of diagonal truncations, and the periodic Wirtinger inequality. For $p>3$, known self-avoidance and regularity results extend the minimisation result to closed rectifiable curves without assuming embeddedness or smoothness, provided the length of the curve image equals $L$. In particular, $M_p$ detects the unknot and is basic for $p>3$, thereby answering a question posed repeatedly in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Scholtes

item.title: The triangular metric on projective surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.16487v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In \cite{ThurstonStretch} Thurston introduced stretch paths and stretch maps between hyperbolic surfaces. In this paper we extend similar constructions to the space of convex real projective structures on surfaces. Using Fock-Goncharov-like parameters, we introduce stretch paths and construct explicit stretch maps between the projective surface. We show that stretch maps are $e^t$--Lipschitz with respect to a triangular metric we introduce on the projective surface. This allows us to gain control on several length functions on an open set of the space of convex real projective structures (those where there is no ``local back--tracking"). As an application we obtain pointwise upper bounds for the Hilbert entropy of some convex real projective structures in terms of Fock-Goncharov-like parameters.
item.dc:creator: Le\'on Carvajales, Xian Dai, Beatrice Pozzetti, Anna Wienhard

item.title: Essential factors for surface homeomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2610.16743v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $f$ be a homeomorphism of a closed orientable surface of genus at least one that is isotopic to a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism, possibly relative to a finite invariant set. We construct an intrinsic monotone factor by collapsing the maximal continua whose iterates have uniformly bounded diameter in the universal cover. The quotient is homeomorphic to the original surface and the factor is isotopic to $f$ and has several strongly chaotic dynamical features. It is infinitely continuum-wise expansive, tight, and topologically mixing, and it has a dense family of rotational horseshoes, dense periodic points, and a single topological homoclinic class. The factor can be taken as an area-preserving homeomorphism. The quotient preserves stable translation length on the fine curve graph and the applicable homological rotation sets. When $f$ is $C^\infty$, a companion paper gives a unique measure of maximal entropy for the factor; it has full support and is Bernoulli.
item.dc:creator: Alejo Garc\'ia-Sassi, F\'abio Tal

item.title: Very high genus double Hurwitz numbers via mixing times
item.description: arXiv:2610.16818v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We obtain very high genus asymptotics for double Hurwitz numbers when both the size $n$ and the genus $g$ go to infinity, under the constraint that $g$ grows much faster than $n$, more precisely that $\frac{2g}{n}-\ln n\to\infty$. Our proof relies on adapting arguments about the mixing time of the transposition random walk introduced by Diaconis and Shahshahani.
item.dc:creator: Baptiste Louf, Lucas Teyssier

item.title: Cohomology ring of the strata of holomorphic differentials of genus 3
item.description: arXiv:2610.17985v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the rational Chow ring of every connected component of the multi-scale compactifications of the genus three strata $\mathcal{H}(4), \mathcal{H}(2,2)$ and $\mathcal{H}(3,1)$ is generated by boundary-stratum classes. Our proof shows Chow-K\"unneth generation property of boundary strata of the multi-scale compactification by reducing the boundary analysis to lower-genus generalized strata of meromorphic differentials, including residueless loci, described through plane-quartic and plane-cubic models. As a consequence, the rational cycle-class map is an isomorphism and the compactifications have no odd rational cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Prabhat Devkota, Myeongjae Lee

item.title: An $SL_2(\mathbb{R}) $-Casson invariant and Reidemeister torsions
item.description: arXiv:2005.06132v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define an $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$-Casson invariant of closed 3-manifolds. We also observe procedures of computing the invariants in terms of Reidemeister torsions. We discuss some approach of giving the Casson invariant some gradings.
item.dc:creator: Takefumi Nosaka

item.title: Twisted local G-wild mapping class groups
item.description: arXiv:2504.01701v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider isomonodromic-deformation parameters of irregular-singular connections on principal G-bundles over complex projective curves: for any connected reductive G, pole order, ramified formal normal form, and twist in the interior of the curve; covering the general setup of meromorphic reductive 2d gauge theory. We focus on the formal moduli, studying the deformation spaces of irregular types/classes at each pole: their fundamental groups are the eponymous local G-wild mapping class groups (G-WMCGs), akin to the complex braid groups of hyperplane arrangements \`a la Brou\'e--Malle--Rouquier. We prove that they sit in exact sequences involving `wild' versions of Weyl groups, and we parameterize their isomorphism classes via `Galois-closed' nested sequences of Levi subcosets \`a la Brou\'e--Malle--Michel. This relies on Lehrer--Springer theory, and in the quasigeneric case yields new modular interpretations of complex reflection groups and of Bessis' braid-group lift. The subregular regime still yields complex reflections in `relative' Springer theory, provided an obstruction vanishes in Howlett theory; but in general one exits the reflection realm. We also introduce new fission trees to treat structure groups of any classical type, after relating with Bell/Stirling numbers, classifying the resulting hyperplane arrangements and describing the local G-WMCGs explicitly. In particular we single out an infinite family of nonreflection examples in type D: they remain K(pi,1) by work of Amend--Deligne--R\"ohrle, fitting the modular viewpoint of `wild' Teichm\"uller spaces in Boalch's theory of wild curves. Finally, we extend all of this to the interior twists. Algebraically, this yields a nonsplit setup where the Weyl group is twisted by an infinitesimal outer automorphism of G, so that fission takes place in a proper reflection coset.
item.dc:creator: Jean Dou\c{c}ot, Gabriele Rembado, Daisuke Yamakawa

item.title: Maps between circle bundles: Fiber-preserving, Finiteness and Realization of mapping degree sets
item.description: arXiv:2505.16285v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $E_i$ be an oriented circle bundle over a closed oriented $n$-manifold $M_i$ with $i=1,2$ and assume that $M_2$ is aspherical. We prove the following geometric realization result, which extends the classical result for maps between circle bundles over surfaces to all dimensions $\geq 2$. Let $f\colon E_1\to E_2$ be a map. If the induced homomorphism $f_*$ on $\pi_1$ sends the fiber subgroup of $\pi_1(E_1)$ to the fiber subgroup of $\pi_1(E_2)$, then there is a fiber-preserving map in the homotopy class of $f$. Using the above result and a computation of the mapping degree set of fiber-preserving maps between $E_1$ and $E_2$, we obtain the following results on the finiteness and the realization problems of mapping degree sets. ($\mathcal F$) The mapping degree set $D(E_1, E_2)$ is finite if $M_2$ is hyperbolic and the Euler class of $E_2$ is not torsion. ($\mathcal R$) For any finite set $A$ of integers containing $0$ and any $n>2$, $A$ is the mapping degree set $D(M,N)$ for some closed oriented $n$-manifolds $M$ and $N$. Item ($\mathcal F$) extends the previously known $3$-dimensional case to all dimensions $\geq 3$. Item ($\mathcal R$) gives a complete answer to the realization problem on finite sets of integers (containing 0) in all dimensions, including in particular the previously unknown cases in dimensions $ 4$ and $5$.
item.dc:creator: Christoforos Neofytidis, Hongbin Sun, Ye Tian, Shicheng Wang, Zhongzi Wang

item.title: Hilbert polynomials of configuration spaces over graphs of circumference at most 1
item.description: arXiv:2505.24416v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $ k $-configuration space $ B_k\Gamma $ of a topological space $ \Gamma $ is the space of sets of $ k $ distinct points in $ \Gamma $. In this paper, we consider the case where $ \Gamma $ is a graph of circumference at most $1$. We show that for all $ k\ge0 $, the $ i $-th Betti number of $ B_k\Gamma $ is given by a polynomial $P_\Gamma^i(k)$ in $ k $, called the Hilbert polynomial of $ \Gamma $. We find an expression for the Hilbert polynomial $P_\Gamma^i(k)$ in terms of those coming from the canonical $1$-bridge decomposition of $ \Gamma $. We also give a combinatorial description of the coefficients of $P_\Gamma^i(k)$.
item.dc:creator: Byung Hee An, Jang Soo Kim

item.title: Properness and finiteness of totally geodesic submanifolds in the convex core
item.description: arXiv:2511.09377v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study totally geodesic submanifolds in the convex core of geometrically finite rank-one locally symmetric manifolds. Although the infinite-volume setting can exhibit highly complicated behavior, including geodesic planes with fractal closures, we show that a strong rigidity persists inside the convex core. This rigidity has striking consequences in the infinite volume setting: every maximal totally geodesic submanifold of dimension at least two contained in the convex core is properly immersed and has finite volume, and only finitely many such submanifolds can occur. These results stand in sharp contrast to the behavior in the finite-volume setting. Moreover, combining this finiteness result with the work of Bader-Fisher-Miller-Stover and of Gromov-Schoen, we deduce that any geometrically finite rank-one manifold with infinitely many maximal totally geodesic submanifolds of dimension at least two and of finite volume must be arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Minju Lee, Hee Oh

item.title: Non-isotopic surfaces in $T^4\#(S^2\times S^2)$: an example
item.description: arXiv:2604.05805v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that there exist infinitely many embedded tori with a common geometric dual in $T^4\#(S^2\times S^2)$ that are homotopic, diffeomorphic, but not isotopic to each other, even after arbitrary many external stabilizations. These surfaces are obtained by applying the Norman trick to a fixed immersed surface, using non-homotopic tubing arcs. The isotopy classes of these surfaces are distinguished by homotopy classes of the 2-handles (relative to the boundary) in the complement of the image of the $0$- and $1$-handles.
item.dc:creator: Jianfeng Lin, Yue Wu

item.title: Triple-cup product forms of 3-manifolds and Heegaard diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2604.13999v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The triple-cup product form $\mu$ is a classical invariant of $3$-manifolds, determining the cohomology ring up to torsion. Given a closed, connected, oriented $3$-manifold $M$, we describe an explicit formula for computing $\mu$ from a Heegaard diagram of $M$. Then, we show that the triple-cup product form $\mu$ can be recovered as a reduction of Turaev's homotopy intersection form $\eta$ of the Heegaard surface.
item.dc:creator: Maya Kayali

item.title: A topological interpretation of numbers
item.description: arXiv:2607.26926v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We survey recent advancements on the realisation problem for mapping degree sets. In particular, we explain that any finite set containing zero is the mapping degree set between some $n$-manifolds, for each $n\geq3$. Our building factors for the construction of the realising manifolds will be aspherical manifolds. Thus, along the way, we review a couple of open questions related to maps of non-zero degree for aspherical manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Christoforos Neofytidis

item.title: Barbell twists are natural
item.description: arXiv:2608.02801v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For any oriented smooth $4$--manifold $X$ diffeomorphic to $(S^2\times D^2)^{\natural n}$ ($n\geq0$), the author establishes a natural isomorphism of abelian groups: $$\mathrm{Mod}(X,\partial X)\cong \mathrm{Mod}(D^4,\partial D^4)\times\wedge^2H_2(X;\mathbb{Z}),$$ concerning the (smooth) boundary-fixing mapping class group of $X$. For $n=2$, the Budney--Gabai barbell twist $\varphi\in\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal{N},\partial\mathcal{N})$ is identified with a generator of the factor subgroup $\wedge^2H_2(\mathcal{N};\mathbb{Z})\cong\mathbb{Z}$. Up to boundary-fixing diffeotopy, the barbell spines of $\mathcal{N}$ are completely classified by the bases of $H_2(\mathcal{N};\mathbb{Z})\cong\mathbb{Z}^2$, forming a homogeneous set modeled on the group $\mathrm{GL}(H_2(\mathcal{N};\mathbb{Z}))\cong\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$. Any barbell spine of $\mathcal{N}$ gives rise to an implanted barbell twist equal to $\varphi$ or $\varphi^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal{N},\partial \mathcal{N})$, according to the sign of the homological basis orientation.
item.dc:creator: Yi Liu

item.title: Gr\"obner Bases for Alexander Fitting Ideals of Links
item.description: arXiv:2608.25725v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multivariable Alexander theory produces Fitting ideals without preferred generators. After fixing a coefficient field and a monomial order, we represent these ideals by reduced Gr\"obner bases of their polynomial contractions, obtaining Alexander--Gr\"obner invariants of links. Over \(\mathbb Q\), for the maximal free-abelian coefficient system of a connected compact oriented \(3\)-manifold whose nonempty boundary is a disjoint union of tori, we deduce determinant-divisor reciprocity from Blanchfield duality. We compute these invariants for torus links and low-crossing links, and we determine \(\AG_2\) for a two-component pretzel family.
item.dc:creator: Takefumi Nosaka, Kotaro Shimizu

item.title: On the Kashaev--Luo--Vartanov Partition Function for Cusped 3-Manifolds: Asymptotics and a squared norm property
item.description: arXiv:2609.33922v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the asymptotic and TQFT-type properties of the Kashaev--Luo--Vartanov (KLV) partition function. We show that the partition function depends on the prescribed angle structure only through its peripheral angular holonomies. For any geometric triangulation of a cusped 3-manifold realizing a possibly incomplete hyperbolic structure, we express the exponential decay rate and the 1-loop term of the partition function in terms of, respectively, the volume and the adjoint twisted Reidemeister torsion of the corresponding incomplete hyperbolic structure. Consequently, these asymptotic formulas hold for any angle structure having the same peripheral angular holonomies as the geometric one. We further introduce a Reshetikhin--Turaev-type function associated with certain admissible Neumann--Zagier data, extending the Jones function in Teichm\"uller TQFT previously studied by Ben Aribi and the author. We show that, after a combinatorial normalization, for any triangulation, the KLV partition function can be expressed as a weighted integral of the squared norm of the Reshetikhin--Turaev-type function, where the weight is determined by the angular holonomies of peripheral curves. In particular, for FAMED triangulations, the Reshetikhin--Turaev-type function agrees with the Jones function, so that the normalized KLV partition function is obtained by integrating the squared norm of the integrand defining the Teichm\"uller TQFT partition function. This provides a noncompact analogue of the relationship between Turaev--Viro and Reshetikhin--Turaev invariants.
item.dc:creator: Ka Ho Wong

item.title: Exotic S^2 x S^2 candidates that are just fake
item.description: arXiv:2610.04634v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that two infinite families of homology $S^2\times S^2$'s presented in \cite{FPS, AP}, originally proposed as exotic candidates, are aspherical. In particular, none of these manifolds is an exotic $S^2\times S^2$. We prove this by reconstructing them from aspherical building blocks, following Edmonds. The same arguments apply to and rule out further candidates for simply connected exotica. We also give counterexamples to the conjecture that Luttinger surgery preserves symplectic asphericity.
item.dc:creator: R. \.{I}nan\c{c} Baykur

item.title: Lagrangian cobordism functor in microlocal sheaf theory I
item.description: arXiv:2108.10914v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a Lagrangian cobordism $L$ of Legendrian submanifolds from $\Lambda_-$ to $\Lambda_+$, we construct a functor $\Phi_L^*: Sh^c_{\Lambda_+}(M) \rightarrow Sh^c_{\Lambda_-}(M) \otimes_{C_{-*}(\Omega_*\Lambda_-)} C_{-*}(\Omega_*L)$ between sheaf categories of compact objects with singular support on $\Lambda_\pm$ and its right adjoint on sheaf categories of proper objects, using Nadler-Shende's work. This gives a sheaf theory description analogous to the Lagrangian cobordism map on Legendrian contact homologies and the right adjoint on their unital augmentation categories. We also deduce some long exact sequences and new obstructions to Lagrangian cobordisms between high dimensional Legendrian submanifolds.
item.dc:creator: Wenyuan Li

item.title: Asymptotics of rational representations for algebraic groups
item.description: arXiv:2405.17360v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the cohomology of subgroups $\Gamma$ of an algebraic group $G$ with coefficients in the various irreducible rational representations of $G$ and raise a conjecture about it. Namely, we expect that the dimensions of these cohomology groups approximate the L2-analogues of Betti numbers of $\Gamma$ with a controlled error term. We provide positive answers when $G$ is a product of copies of $SL_2$.
item.dc:creator: Lander Guerrero S\'anchez, Henrique Souza

item.title: On hidden face contributions of configuration space integrals for long embeddings
item.description: arXiv:2410.13168v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Configuration space integrals are powerful tools for studying the homotopy type of the space of long embeddings in terms of a combinatorial object called a graph complex. It is unknown whether these integrals give a cochain map due to potential obstructions called hidden faces. The purpose of this paper is to address these hidden faces by modifying configuration space integrals: we incorporate the acyclic bar complex of some dg algebra into the original graph complex, without changing its cohomology. Then, we give a cochain map from the new graph complex to the de Rham complex of the space of long embeddings modulo immersions, by combining the original configuration space integrals with Chen's iterated integrals. As the original complex, we choose a modified graph complex so that it is quasi-isomorphic to both the hairy graph complex and a graph complex introduced in the context of embedding calculus.
item.dc:creator: Leo Yoshioka

item.title: Some non-trivial cycles of the space of long embeddings detected by configuration space integral invariants using g-loop (g =2, 3) graphs
item.description: arXiv:2502.12547v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we give some non-trivial geometric cycles of the space of long embeddings R^j --> R^n (n-j >= 2) modulo immersions. We construct a class of cycles from specific chord diagrams associated with 2-loop or 3-loop hairy graphs. To detect these cycles, we use cocycles obtained by the 2-loop or 3-loop part of modified configuration space integrals using a modified Bott-Cattaneo-Rossi graph complex. We show the non-triviality of the cycles by pairing argument, which is reduced to pairing of graphs with the chord diagrams. As a corollary of the 2-loop part, we provide an alternative proof of the non-finite generation of the (j-1)-th rational homotopy group of the space of long embeddings of codimension two, which Budney--Gabai and Watanabe first established. We also show the non-finite generation of the 2(j-1)-th homotopy group by using the 3-loop part.
item.dc:creator: Leo Yoshioka

item.title: Modular fusion categories with trivial Torelli group actions
item.description: arXiv:2608.04462v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study modular fusion categories whose mapping class group representations are trivial on the Torelli groups, with particular emphasis on the congruence properties of the resulting representations of $\mathrm{Sp}(2g, \mathbb{Z})$. We prove that, for any $g \ge 3$, the Torelli group is contained in the kernel of the genus-$g$ mapping class group representation $\rho_g$ associated with a modular fusion category $\mathcal{C}$ if and only if $\mathcal{C}$ is pointed. This refines the corresponding result in \cite{MW25}. We also characterize the modular fusion categories for which the genus-$2$ Torelli group is contained in $\ker \rho_2$; in particular, categories with isotropic adjoint subcategories belong to this class. Finally, we give a complete classification of modular fusion categories with isotropic adjoint subcategories, and determine the groups $G$ satisfying $\mathcal{Z}(\mathrm{Vect}_G)$ is 2-Torelli trivial but $\mathcal{Z}(\mathrm{Vect}_G)_{\mathrm{ad}}$ is not isotropic are precisely 2-Engel groups of nilpotent class 3.
item.dc:creator: Liang Chang, Siu-Hung Ng, Yilong Wang

item.title: Overlap-Helly theorems
item.description: arXiv:2609.10023v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we introduce a generalization of Helly's theorem closely connected to B\'ar\'any-Gromov overlap theorems (also called selection lemmas). Our main result implies both the topological colorful Helly of Kalai and Meschulam and Karasev's topological centerpoint theorem. We further investigate the topological fractional Helly theorem from this overlap perspective, and show an overlap theorem for dense complexes (a continuous second selection lemma for tame maps).
item.dc:creator: Andreas F. Holmsen, Alfredo Hubard

item.title: Braid Stability and a Floer theory of Braid Isotopies
item.description: arXiv:2609.34961v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We build a Floer theory on the space of braids of periodic orbits of a Hamiltonian flow on a closed symplectic surface. The differential and continuation maps are defined by counting Floer isotopies of braids: tuples of Floer cylinders with pairwise disjoint graphs. With this new perspective, we prove a quantitative braid stability result that shows the persistence of braids under possibly large Hamiltonian perturbations. As an application, we show that for every $\alpha\geq 0$ there is a sequence of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms $\phi_k$ on the two-torus $T^2$ such that $$d_H(\operatorname{Ent}_{\leq \alpha}(T^2,\omega),\phi_k)\to \infty \quad (k \to \infty),$$ where $\text{Ent}_{\leq \alpha}(T^2,\omega)\subset \text{Ham}(T^2,\omega)$ denotes the set of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms with topological entropy at most $\alpha$ and $d_H$ the Hofer metric. We prove this result by studying only contractible periodic orbits, whereas analogous higher-genus statements were previously obtained using non-contractible orbits.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Grunder

item.title: Mock Modularity, Resurgence, and Dual False Theta Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.00516v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The $\hat{Z}$ invariant of a three-manifold $M_{3}$, a half-index of the $3d$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ theory $T[M_{3}]$, is well understood for negative-definite plumbed three-manifolds. For orientation-reversed manifolds, however, the known formulas fail to produce $q$-series, and making sense of the operation $q \rightarrow q^{-1}$ remains a central open problem. Seifert manifolds, whose $\hat{Z}$ invariants are built from false theta functions, offer a natural testing ground. We study ``dual false theta functions'', the objects that should replace false theta functions under orientation reversal. Two characterizations of these duals exist in the literature: a modular one, based on mock modularity with a prescribed shadow, and a resurgent one, based on Borel--Mordell integrals and transseries. We prove that the two characterizations are equivalent. We construct a new family of dual false theta functions for values of positive integer $p$ satisfying a Pell-equation condition. Its members are built from Zwegers' indefinite theta functions, have integer coefficients, and have effective central charge $c_{\text{eff}} \leq 1$. We also show that the mock theta functions of Li and Schwagenscheidt satisfy these characterizations and arise from a natural regularization of the divergent product $\eta^{3}(\tau)\psi_{p, a}(- \tau)$.
item.dc:creator: Mrunmay Jagadale

item.title: Homotopy Self-Equivalences of Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.02244v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hambleton and Kreck described the group of based homotopy self-equivalences of a closed oriented $4$-manifold by a commutative braid of exact sequences built from bordism groups and the Postnikov $2$-type. We construct the analogous braid for closed oriented $BO\langle n+1\rangle$-manifolds $M$ of dimension $2n$ or $2n-1$ whose fundamental group is finite or infinite cyclic and which satisfy one condition on the action of $\pi_1$ on the homotopy of the fibre of $M\to P_n(M)$. We compute $\operatorname{Aut}_\bullet(S^1\times S^{m-1})\cong(\mathbb{Z}/2)^2$ for $m\ge4$, and $\operatorname{Aut}_\bullet(S^3\times S^3)\cong(\mathbb{Z}/12)^2\rtimes SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ with the standard action modulo $12$. Further, $\operatorname{Aut}_\bullet(S^3\times S^4)\cong(\mathbb{Z}/2\oplus\mathbb{Z}/24)\rtimes(\mathbb{Z}/2)^2$ has order $192$, that $\operatorname{Aut}_\bullet(S^4\times S^4)\cong D_4\times\mathbb{Z}/2$ has order $16$, and that for connected sums of $r\ge2$ copies of $S^3\times S^3$ the kernel contains a subgroup $(\mathbb{Z}/12)^{2r}$ on which the permutations of the summands act non-trivially. For $S^p\times S^p$ the kernel is a sum of two copies of $\pi_{2p}(S^p)$ modulo Whitehead products with $\iota_p$, and the image is determined by an obstruction on the Whitehead square. In particular $\operatorname{Aut}_\bullet(S^5\times S^5)$ is isomorphic to the theta subgroup of $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and $\operatorname{Aut}_\bullet(S^7\times S^7)$ is an extension of $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ by $(\mathbb{Z}/120)^2$.
item.dc:creator: Mehmetcik Pamuk

item.title: Symplectic symmetries of a hypothetical exotic $CP^2$: a potential construction or a nonexistence proof
item.description: arXiv:2610.06746v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper is primarily concerned with the existence of a symplectic $4$-manifold, homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to $CP^2$, which admits a nontrivial finite order symplectomorphism. We reduced the existence of such an exotic $CP^2$ to a question in contact geometry. More concretely, we showed that there are precisely $12$ plumbed manifolds, each equipped with a canonical contact structure associated to the plumbing, such that an exotic $CP^2$ with a nontrivial finite order symplectomorphism exists if and only if one of the $12$ contact plumbed manifolds admits a certain specific symplectic filling. As the main technical result, we completely determined the order and local representations of a pseudofree symplectic $Z_p$-action for an odd prime $p$ on a rational homology $CP^2$ with positive canonical class. Our result suggests that potentially, there are symplectic $Z_p$-actions which are not a finite automorphism of a fake projective plane. Moreover, we introduced a construction, which, under the minimal assumptions on the symplectic fillings of the $12$ contact plumbed manifolds, produces a symplectic $4$-manifold on the Bogomolov-Miyaoka-Yau line via a reverse-engineering process.
item.dc:creator: Weimin Chen

item.title: Bi-contact plugs and dynamical hyperbolicity
item.description: arXiv:2610.11243v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a theory of bi-contact plugs on oriented $3$-manifolds to construct Anosov flows or, more generally, structurally stable nonsingular flows. For a hyperbolic plug with filling Morse-Smale boundary laminations, we prove that every strongly transverse gluing map can be isotoped through strongly transverse maps to identify a strongly adapted unoriented contact form. The resulting flow is hyperbolic and is Anosov when the quotient is closed. This answers a question of B\'eguin-Bonatti-Yu. The result also extends to gluing nonsingular partially hyperbolic flows. Anosov completion by reflection embeds each such hyperbolic plug in an Anosov flow on its oriented double. Further applications include a classification of structurally generic projectively Anosov flows without saddle periodic orbits and Morse-Smale examples with prescribed saddle count. Generalizing the construction of Bonatti-Bowden-Potrie, finite capping embeds any bi-contact plug in a closed projectively Anosov flow with the same topological entropy, preserving partial hyperbolicity for attracting plugs. We also construct flows with controlled invariant torus dynamics on torus bundles and on doubles of plugs with coorientable boundary bi-foliations. Finally, every cooriented partially hyperbolic bi-contact plug admits a Liouville structure on its thickening, with Liouville trajectories projecting to positively reparametrized flow lines. Repelling plugs yield four-dimensional Liouville domains, often with chaotic skeletons.
item.dc:creator: Surena Hozoori
